description: Mohataz Hossain used IESVE to model an existing garment factory in Bangladesh and assess thermal-comfort improvements. The account describes building geometry, dynamic thermal simulation and computational fluid dynamics using ModelIT, ApacheSim, MacroFlo and MicroFlo. Weather and operational field measurements supported model calibration. Scenarios varied daytime and nighttime ventilation, window openings and internal layout to compare possible retrofit measures. The source gives inconsistent university affiliations, Birmingham and Nottingham, so neither is adopted. The factory name and full study period are unspecified. This public HTML case narrative is published by IES and can be read without payment. Its reuse licence is not stated. Access to the described software, input data and project models is not established by the public page. The source does not give a complete study period or all spatial and temporal model resolutions. Reported results are provider claims and have not been independently reproduced. The case supports the documented infrastructure simulation use and is linked to the named modelling resources. Only metadata and the case description were inspected; no data or model files were downloaded.
